rows.grounds: first member of pair with mukti
second member of pair with bhukti
denotes those to whom one becomes dear

items.question: What attainment makes one dear to the yoginīs?
premises: Enjoyment and liberation are named together.
Great accomplishment is the subject.
Becoming dear to the yoginīs is the stated result.
items.inference: One who attains great accomplishment in enjoyment and liberation becomes dear to the yoginīs.
items.plain_english: One may become dear to the yoginīs through the great accomplishment of enjoyment and liberation.

rows.grounds: describes the chapter as issued forth

items.question: Which chapter concludes with emergence in Candra-dvīpa?
premises: A place named Candra-dvīpa is mentioned.
Emergence in that place is indicated.
The ninth chapter is identified.
items.inference: The ninth chapter is the one that has emerged in Candra-dvīpa.
items.plain_english: Thus the ninth chapter, emerged in Candra-dvīpa, is concluded.

rows.grounds: agent or instrument surrounding the self
describes the self as encircled by fire
describes the posture of the self

items.question: How should the practitioner visualize the self in this fiery posture?
premises: The self is surrounded by fire.
The self is described as standing.
The stance is on one foot.
items.inference: The practitioner should visualize the self encircled by fire and standing on one foot.
items.plain_english: Visualize the self surrounded by fire, standing on one foot.

rows.grounds: specifies what is to be determined

items.question: What request is made to the deity regarding the determination of knowledge?
premises: The determination of knowledge is sought.
The deity is directly addressed.
The speaker asks for it to be made manifest now.
items.inference: The speaker asks the deity to reveal the determination of knowledge at this time.
items.plain_english: O God, make manifest to me today the determination of knowledge.

items.question: What division of octads does the speaker seek to know fully?
premises: A division of eight groups of eight is named.
The aim is full knowledge of that division.
The knowing is sought in an exhaustive manner.
items.inference: The speaker seeks to know fully and exhaustively the division into eight groups of eight.
uncertainties: anantathā may mean endlessly or in infinite detail
items.plain_english: And to know fully, in endless detail, the division into eight groups of eight.

items.question: How is the wheel in the secret place said to be accomplished?
premises: A secret place is identified as a wheel.
Accomplishment of this wheel is asserted.
The accomplishment occurs quickly.
items.inference: The wheel in the secret place is accomplished quickly.
items.plain_english: O Bhairava, tell how the wheel in the secret place is quickly accomplished.

rows.grounds: first member indicating rarity among gods

items.question: Why does Bhairava approve the goddess’s question about this teaching?
premises: Bhairava expresses strong approval.
He states he has been asked.
The matter asked about is hard to obtain even for the gods.
items.inference: Bhairava approves because the goddess has asked about a teaching rare even among the gods.
items.plain_english: Well said, well said, O Great Goddess; I have been asked about something hard to obtain even for the gods.

rows.grounds: location or identity assigned to kṣa

items.question: Where are the syllables kṣa and laṃ located in the subtle body?
premises: The syllable kṣa is associated with the brahmarandhra.
The syllable laṃ is named next.
The syllable laṃ is located in the forehead.
items.inference: The syllable kṣa is placed at the brahmarandhra and the syllable laṃ in the forehead.
uncertainties: lalāṭayoḥ is dual in form though translated as forehead region
items.plain_english: The syllable kṣa is in the brahmarandhra, and the syllable laṃ is in the forehead.

items.question: Where are the syllables ṣa and śa placed in the body?
premises: The syllable ṣa is assigned to the throat region.
The syllable śa is named after it.
The syllable śa is assigned to the heart.
items.inference: The syllable ṣa is placed in the throat region and the syllable śa in the heart.
items.plain_english: Then the syllable ṣa is in the throat region, and the syllable śa is in the heart.

rows.grounds: states that the wheels have been taught

items.question: What instruction follows the declaration of the place-wheels?
premises: The place-wheels have been declared.
Their meditation is now offered as the topic.
The beloved is commanded to listen.
items.inference: After declaring the place-wheels, the teaching turns to their meditation and asks the beloved to hear it.
items.plain_english: Thus the place-wheels have been declared; now hear their meditation, O beloved.

rows.grounds: first member indicating number of spokes

items.question: How is the divine lotus of the first octad described?
premises: A divine lotus is described.
The lotus has eight spokes or petals.
It is adorned by the first octad.
items.inference: The divine lotus is eight-spoked and adorned by the first octad.
uncertainties: āraṃ may indicate spokes or divisions
items.plain_english: Meditate on the divine eight-spoked lotus, adorned by the first octad.

rows.grounds: first member of social conduct to abandon

items.question: What conduct should a practitioner abandon after gaining mental equipoise through practice?
premises: Practice leads to an equal or balanced mind.
Village dharma is named as something to renounce.
Abandonment is prescribed.
items.inference: Through practice, one with a balanced mind should abandon conventional village dharma.
uncertainties: grāma-dharmañ may refer to worldly or social duties
items.plain_english: Through practice, with mind made even, one should abandon the ways of worldly life.

rows.grounds: power to immobilize bonds or foes

items.question: What powers arise from this practice according to the teaching?
premises: Knowledge of hearing from afar is named.
Paralysis of bonds is named.
These are presented as attained results.
items.inference: The practice yields knowledge of distant hearing and the power to paralyze bonds.
uncertainties: pāśa-stobham may mean paralysis of bonds or immobilization by bonds
items.plain_english: O beloved, one gains knowledge of distant hearing and likewise the power to paralyze bonds.

items.question: What further attainments are summarized for the goddess in this context?
premises: Immortality is named as an attainment.
Transformation is also named.
The teaching states these in brief.
items.inference: In brief, the attainments include immortality and transformation.
uncertainties: parivartanam could mean transformation or reversal depending on context
items.plain_english: O Goddess, in brief, there is immortality and likewise transformation.

rows.grounds: describes the lotus as brightly lit

items.question: How is the second eight-petaled center characterized in meditation?
premises: A second center is introduced.
It is eight-petaled.
It is well illuminated by meditation on fire.
items.inference: The second eight-petaled center is brightly illuminated through fiery meditation.
items.plain_english: The second is an eight-petaled lotus, well illuminated by meditation on fire.

items.question: What ability arises for one whose mind is absorbed in one-pointed meditation?
premises: The mind is absorbed in one-pointed meditation.
Form is produced as a result.
The form can be made in many ways.
items.inference: One whose mind is absorbed in one-pointed meditation can assume many forms.
items.plain_english: One whose mind is absorbed in one-pointed meditation can assume many forms.

rows.grounds: condition under which power is exercised

items.question: What destructive power is attributed to the practitioner when angered?
premises: The practitioner is described as angry.
The power to destroy is asserted.
The entire triple world, moving and unmoving, is the scope.
items.inference: When angered, the practitioner may destroy the entire triple world with all moving and unmoving beings.
items.plain_english: When angry, he can destroy the whole triple world, with all that moves and does not move.

items.question: What liberating function is attributed to the third great wheel?
premises: A third great wheel is introduced.
Nine tattvas are specified.
The wheel is described as a liberator.
items.inference: The third great wheel functions as the liberator from the nine tattvas.
items.plain_english: The third great wheel is the liberator from the nine principles.

items.question: What bodily and perceptual benefits result from this wheel’s practice?
premises: Destruction of wrinkles and grey hair is named.
Seeing from very far away is named.
Both are presented as attained results.
items.inference: The practice removes wrinkles and grey hair and grants vision from very far away.
items.plain_english: It brings the destruction of wrinkles and grey hair, and likewise the ability to see from very far away.

items.question: How should one practice meditation in solitude to assume many forms?
premises: Practice is to be done in solitude.
Many forms are to be made.
One must be intent on meditation.
items.inference: In solitude, intent on meditation, one should practice making many forms.
items.plain_english: In solitude, intent on meditation, make many forms through that practice.

items.question: What condition enables the practitioner to achieve immortality through this discipline?
premises: Immortality is achieved.
Constant practice is required.
The practitioner must be intent on that practice.
items.inference: One intent on constant practice indeed achieves immortality.
items.plain_english: Indeed, one intent on constant practice attains immortality.

items.question: What effect does abstaining from food by day have on age and death?
premises: Non-eating by day is specified.
Age-related death is named.
A future going beyond it is stated.
items.inference: By abstaining from food during the day, one will overcome death from aging.
uncertainties: gamiṣyate with mṛtyuṃ is ambiguous; may mean go to or go beyond death
items.plain_english: By not eating during the day, one will overcome death brought by age.

items.question: What bodily form results from constant yogic practice over time?
premises: Constant practice through yoga is the means.
A span of sixteen years is indicated.
A resulting form is attained.
items.inference: Through constant yogic practice, one may attain the form of a sixteen-year-old.
items.plain_english: Through constant yogic practice, one may attain the form of a sixteen-year-old.

items.question: What power arises from continually contemplating a smoke-colored form?
premises: A smoke-colored object is to be contemplated.
The contemplation is continual.
The triple world is affected as a result.
items.inference: By continually contemplating a smoke-colored form, one may shake the triple world.
items.plain_english: O beloved, by always contemplating a smoke-colored form, one can shake the triple world.
